data.narrative:
Climeworks, a Series F direct air capture company founded by Christoph Gebald and Jan Wurzbacher, is evaluated against a fragmented Climate & Energy peer universe of 9 private and 1 public comparable (Lanzatech, LNZA). The sector remains characterized by high capital intensity and long commercialization timelines, limiting the availability of directly analogous companies at identical stages.

The valuation analysis applied stage-progression methodology, the sole applicable triangulation approach given insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage peer density in the Climate & Energy space. Using total capital raised ($1.0B+) as a valuation proxy and applying a typical Series F step-up multiplier of 1.3x yields an implied value of $1.3B. A peer-median approach was not viable; while the broader Climate & Energy sector contains 9 comparables, filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier companies produced fewer than three datapoints, rendering median triangulation unreliable and subject to undue noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $1.1B to $1.5B, with a central estimate of $1.3B. Key uncertainties include commercialization risk inherent to early-stage carbon removal, capital requirements for scaling direct air capture infrastructure, and regulatory/carbon market policy trajectories. The single-method foundation reflects genuine peer-set constraints rather than analytical confidence, and future rounds with materialized revenue or operational milestones would substantially sharpen precision.
